content.text:
Step s3 is done. I ran the simulation for all three candidates at 2, 5 and 10 cm, and recorded the results.

| Crystal | 2 cm | 5 cm | 10 cm |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | 3.25% | **3.03%** | 4.22% |
| K2 | 5.35% | **4.45%** | 6.35% |
| K3 | 9.80% | **9.10%** | 11.90% |

*FWHM at 662 keV, 100,000 events per run.*

- **Best thickness:** every crystal is best at 5 cm. Resolution gets worse at 10 cm, by about 31–43% relative to 5 cm.
- **Best crystal:** K1 is best at every thickness tested.
- **Consistency with the 2025 simulation:** the 5 cm results match the earlier nominal values for K1 (2.9% vs 3.03%) and K2 (4.5% vs 4.45%). K3 comes out about 7% higher (8.5% vs 9.10%).
- **Optical assumptions:** the 2025 summary gives no optical or light-collection assumptions. It only says thickness dependence is weak over 3–8 cm. The 10 cm degradation therefore cannot be checked against a documented assumption. It is plausibly light-collection or attenuation loss over the longer path, but that is unverified.
- **Low-background check:** still open. No document gives radiopurity data for K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or the Th/U chains, so none of the three candidates has been cleared on that basis yet.

I recorded all nine values, along with these caveats, for the later steps.

The 10 cm results look anomalous: all three crystals degrade by 31–43% relative to 5 cm, which doesn't match the 2025 "weak thickness dependence" note. I'll rerun the K1 points at 5 and 10 cm to confirm before deciding.

The reruns reproduce the pattern: K1 at 10 cm is still about 43% worse than at 5 cm, so the degradation is real and not a single-run fluke. Run-to-run scatter is about 0.2 percentage points. I'll record the decision.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Crystal-K1 at 5 cm**, conditional on a radiopurity check.

- **Resolution:** K1 is best at every thickness tested. At 5 cm it gives 3.03% FWHM at 662 keV (2.83% on rerun). The next best is K2 at 4.45%, and K3 is at 9.10%.
- **Thickness:** 5 cm is the optimum for all three crystals. Both 2 cm and 10 cm are worse.
- **Anomaly check:** I reran K1 at 5 and 10 cm because the 10 cm degradation (31–43%) was unexpectedly large. The reruns reproduced it (4.03% at 10 cm versus 2.83% at 5 cm), so I treated it as real. I could not confirm the physical cause, because the documents give no optical or light-collection assumptions.
- **Trade-offs:** a 10 cm crystal worsens resolution and adds more volume, which means more internal background and more mass. A 2 cm crystal is less efficient and resolves worse. I did not simulate efficiency, so the efficiency trade-off is qualitative only.
- **Low-background compliance is unverified.** No project document gives K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or Th/U data for any candidate. K1 is chosen on resolution alone. Vendor radiopurity certification is needed before procurement. If K1 fails it, the fallback is K2 at 5 cm (4.45%).

The configuration and justification are recorded.

No project document gives K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or Th/U contamination data, a background budget, or radiopurity limits for any candidate, so K1 was selected on resolution alone. content.text:
I recorded the final recommendation: **Crystal-K1 at 5 cm**, with a FWHM of 3.03% at 662 keV (2.83% on the best rerun).

- **Resolution:** K1 is the best of the three candidates at every thickness tested. 5 cm is the best thickness for all three crystals. The fallback, K2 at 5 cm, gives 4.45%.
- **Low-background suitability is not verified.** No project document gives K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or Th/U data for any candidate, and there is no background budget. K1 was chosen on resolution alone. Vendor radiopurity certification for K1 is needed before procurement. If K1 fails, switch to K2 at 5 cm.
- **Shielding and radon control** (20 cm lead, 5 cm OFHC copper, nitrogen radon purge) are already in place.
- **Open caveats:** efficiency was not simulated. The 10 cm degradation reproduced on rerun, but its physical cause is undocumented. A 10 cm crystal would also add internal background by volume.

input.justification: Crystal-K1 at 5 cm gives the best 662 keV FWHM of the three candidates: 3.03% in the original run and 2.83% on rerun. K1 was the best candidate at 2, 5 and 10 cm, and 5 cm was the best thickness for all three crystals. The 10 cm result was reproduced on rerun (4.03% vs 2.83% at 5 cm), so the degradation is treated as real, though its physical cause is undocumented. Low-background suitability is NOT verified. No project document gives K-40, La-138, Lu-176 or Th/U data, a background budget, or radiopurity limits for any candidate, so this recommendation rests on resolution alone. Vendor radiopurity certification for K1 is required before procurement. If K1 fails that check, the fallback is K2 at 5 cm (4.45% FWHM). K3 is not recommended (9.10%). Efficiency was not simulated. Shielding (20 cm Pb, 5 cm OFHC Cu) and the boil-off nitrogen radon purge are already in place. Note that K1's high light yield and fast decay do not by themselves establish radiopurity, and high-light-yield scintillators can carry intrinsic activity, so the certification check is the decisive step.
